text: Macanal is a town and municipality in the Colombian Department of Boyacá, situated within the Neira Province subregion. Its urban center lies in the Tenza Valley in the Eastern Ranges of the Colombian Andes at an elevation of 1,680.3 meters (5,513 ft), although parts of the municipality extend to 2,500 meters (8,200 ft). It shares borders with Campohermoso to the east, Almeida to the west, Garagoa to the north, and Santa María and Chivor to the south. The name Macanal is either derived from the Chibcha word Macana, meaning garrote, or from the Macana palm tree (Wettinia kalbreyeri). Historically, the area was part of the Muisca Confederation, where the zaque of Hunza held authority over Macanal. Modern Macanal was officially founded on May 4, 1807. The municipality is renowned for its natural beauty, eco-tourism, and outdoor activities, with key attractions including the Chivor Reservoir—popular for kayaking, fishing, and kite surfing—as well as nearby waterfalls and hiking trails. It is also a prime destination for birdwatching, featuring a variety of native and migratory bird species. Rural tourism and local festivals that celebrate regional culture are also available. The Reinado del Agua, a cultural and tourist event in Macanal, Boyacá, honors the municipality’s water resources, particularly the Chivor Reservoir, through parades, folk performances, sports, and musical events, emphasizing environmental awareness and water conservation. The event also showcases traditional gastronomy and handicrafts, reinforcing cultural identity and supporting sustainable tourism. The Macanal Formation, an organic shale, is found in the area and has been named after the municipality. The main economic activities in Macanal include agriculture such as coffee (Coffea arabica), bananas, maize, beans (Phaseolus vulgaris), yuca, sugarcane (Saccharum officinarum), arracacha (Arracacia xanthorrhiza), avocados, papayas, mangoes, guayaba, and cucumbers (Cucumis sativus and Cyclanthera pedata), as well as livestock farming and mining of gypsum and emeralds. Its geographic coordinates are 4°58′19″N 73°19′10″W (4.97194°N 73.31944°W).
